newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank sees 1997 core inflation +5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank sees 1997 core inflation +5.0 pct.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Thursday it expected 1997 core inflation to grow 5.0 percent, while regulated prices such as energy jumped 15.2 percent.
The CNB said in the statement that it expected foodstuff prices to rise 7.0 percent.
The CNB said it expected 1997 industrial producer prices to rise 4.0 percent.
"The economic policy must be very credible. I would not like to see this year any sort of excesses," Tosovsky told a news conference in response to a question concerning the deregulation of prices.
The CNB has pegged its 1997 inflation target at 7.9 percent, though it is dependent on the government holding to its stated price regulation and deregulation programme.
Average 1996 annual inflation was 8.8 percent, after 9.1 percent in 1995. The year-on-yaer inflation rate for 1996 was 8.6 percent.
